chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The length of the wall of the Messenger of Allah's (peace be upon him and his family) mosque was a qamah (a standing man's height). So he (peace be upon him) would say to Bilal: 'When the time enters, O Bilal, ascend above the wall and raise your voice with the Adhan. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has assigned a wind to carry the Adhan to the sky. And indeed, when the angels hear the Adhan from the people of the earth, they say: 'These are the voices of the ummah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the Tawhid of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' And they seek forgiveness for the ummah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) until they finish from that prayer.'

key_terms.بِلَالٍ: Bilal ibn Rabah, the companion known for his beautiful voice and role as the first Mu'adhdhin

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet instruct Bilal to raise his voice during the Adhan?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the physical height of the Prophet’s mosque wall to the acoustic practice of raising the voice in Adhan. The hadith elaborates on the metaphysical dimension of the call, describing how a divine wind carries the Adhan to the heavens where angels affirm the monotheism of the Ummah and intercede for them, a concept often cited by Shia jurists to support the recommendation of *Ighlaq* (raising the voice) in the Adhan.
